title: ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR STARTUPS
body_text:
Under the Ministry of Textile's National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), the scheme of "Grant for Research and Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Technical Textiles (GREAT)" aims to support the start-up ecosystem in the technical textiles sector across the country, including Telangana, by providing assistance to young innovators, scientists, technologists, and start-up ventures in translating their ideas into commercial technologies and products. The total budget allocated to the NTTM for the current financial year (2026-27) is Rs. 256 crore, which includes the provision for releasing grants to start-ups under the GREAT scheme.
Under NTTM, 15 research projects and 01 application from an educational institution under the "General Guidelines for Enabling of Academic Institutes in Technical Textiles Education in India: For Private and Public Institutes" have been approved from the State of Telangana.
An Evaluation and Monitoring Committee (EMC) has been constituted under NTTM to evaluate, monitor, and review the technical and financial parameters of the start-up proposals. Based on the criteria laid out in the GREAT guidelines, the EMC submits its recommendations to the Empowered Programme Committee (EPC) under NTTM for approval of start-up proposals. GREAT guidelines are available at https://nttm.texmin.gov.in.
The grants provided to start-ups under NTTM are aimed at promoting innovation, commercialization of indigenous technologies, and the development of value-added technical textile products. The anticipated economic impact of these grants is fundamentally driven by robust collaborations between the supported start-ups and established industry partners. By fostering strong synergies between innovators and industry stakeholders for prototype development, field trials, and market launches, the scheme ensures market-ready commercialization. This active industry engagement is anticipated to successfully scale these start-ups, significantly strengthen the overall technical textiles ecosystem in the country, and thereby catalyze broader sustainable industry growth and employment generation.
Under NTTM, a total of 31 start-ups have been approved at a total cost of Rs 15.40 crore, of which Rs 13.65 crore is the Government of India share, details of which are given below.
Under NTTM, a Review and Monitoring Committee has been constituted to assess and oversee the progress of the approved start-ups, with the authority to recommend for release of subsequent instalments of grant and closure of projects to the Empowered Programme Committee. Further, various public events, workshops, seminars and outreach activities are being organized nationwide to disseminate information about the scheme and facilitate industry engagement for scaling up the potential start-up projects.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Textiles informed the Lok Sabha that under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), the GREAT scheme has approved 31 start-up projects at a total cost of Rs 15.40 crore, of which Rs 13.65 crore is the Government of India's share. The NTTM's total budget for 2026-27 is Rs 256 crore, and Telangana alone has had 15 research projects and one academic institution application approved under related NTTM guidelines. The information was given by Minister of State for Textiles Shri Pabitra Margherita in a written reply.
enrichment.context: The National Technical Textiles Mission was launched by the Government of India in 2020 with a four-year outlay to position India as a global leader in technical textiles—a sunrise sector encompassing agrotech, meditech, geotech, mobiltech, protech, and other advanced textile applications used in defence, healthcare, infrastructure, and space technology. The Mission has components for research and development, promotion of market development, export promotion, and education/skill development, aiming to increase India's share in the global technical textiles market and boost domestic manufacturing under the Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives. The GREAT (Grant for Research and Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Technical Textiles) scheme specifically targets the start-up ecosystem, encouraging innovators, scientists, and technologists to convert research ideas into commercially viable products through structured government grants and industry linkages. This initiative fits into the broader Startup India ecosystem and reflects the government's push to integrate niche high-value manufacturing sectors with an innovation and entrepreneurship framework, supported by institutional mechanisms like the Evaluation and Monitoring Committee (EMC), Empowered Programme Committee (EPC), and Review and Monitoring Committee to ensure accountability and progress tracking of funded projects.
